draft.title: The world's oldest continuing cultures
card: First Nations Australians have the oldest continuing cultures on Earth. Their cultures have been carried on for tens of thousands of years.
Continuing does not mean unchanged. Practices have been passed down through generations and have also changed over time as people adapted to new conditions.
a natural earth pigment, usually red or yellow. It has been used for tens of thousands of years, for example in art and ceremony.
images painted, drawn or engraved on rock. It is still made and cared for today, and the styles and subjects have changed over time.
draft.remember: Old practices such as ochre and rock art are carried on and also change.

a.q: Which statement best explains why First Nations Australian cultures are called continuing cultures?
opts: Practices were passed down and adapted over time
Practices stayed exactly the same over all that time
Practices were lost, then found again by researchers
Practices are now found only in museums and shelters
a.why: Continuing means practices have been handed on through generations while also changing as people adapted. Saying they stayed exactly the same is tempting, but the card says continuing does not mean unchanged.

b.q: A guide at a rock art site says, 'Artists here still paint today, though their styles differ from those of long ago.' What does this show about the culture?
opts: A practice can be carried on and change at the same time
The culture must have ended and then restarted
The old art has no link to the art made today
The culture has changed so much that it is a new one
b.why: Artists still paint, so the practice has been carried on, and the styles differ, so it has changed. The last option is tempting, but change over time does not mean a culture has stopped being continuing.
b.clue: Look at both parts of what the guide says.

a.best: Practices were passed down and adapted over time

b.best: A practice can be carried on and change at the same time

problems.detail: Why (b) calls 'the last option' tempting, but options are shuffled. Its reasoning ('change over time does not mean a culture has stopped being continuing') answers 'The culture has changed so much that it is a new one', not 'The culture must have ended and then restarted'. The explanation may point students at the wrong distractor.

The right option is the only one hedged with 'can' and almost repeats the remember line ('carried on and also change'). The distractors use absolutes ('must', 'no link', 'so much'), so a student could pick it without understanding the idea.
